forgotten-realms.place.dancing-dell.who_may: Drow who worship Eilistraee often dance there.
forgotten-realms.place.dancing-dell.combines: The Ladystone’s powers protect it; the goddess may manifest.

forgotten-realms.place.castle-grimstead.name: Castle Grimstead

effect.summary: A ruined keep in western Shadowdale whose cellars connect through drow passages toward an underground lake and the Underdark.

forgotten-realms.place.castle-grimstead.combines: Cellars connect to the Twisted Tower’s cellars.

effect.summary: A region north of which Castle Grimstead lies.

forgotten-realms.place.castle-spulzeer.name: Castle Spulzeer

effect.summary: A vanished keep in Spulzeer Vale associated with dangerous legends and possible hidden ruins.

forgotten-realms.place.castle-spulzeer.who_may: Adventurers in the area have vanished.
forgotten-realms.place.castle-spulzeer.combines: Legends mention a moonlight-visible city cloaked by a mythal.

forgotten-realms.place.spulzeer-vale.name: Spulzeer Vale

effect.summary: An overgrown valley in eastern Amn that contained Castle Spulzeer.

forgotten-realms.place.spulzeer-vale.who_may: Elves and wild animals avoid it.

forgotten-realms.place.cavern-of-death.name: Cavern of Death

effect.summary: A stream-cut cave network serving as the lich Asbaron’s guarded home.

forgotten-realms.place.cavern-of-death.go_wrong: Monsters may be unleashed into the Stonelands.
forgotten-realms.place.cavern-of-death.combines: Asbaron keeps monsters gathered from across Faerûn.

forgotten-realms.place.caverns-of-the-cl.name: Caverns of the Claws

effect.summary: A simple cavern complex repeatedly occupied by trolls.

forgotten-realms.place.caverns-of-the-cl.cost_or_limit: Trolls return despite repeated patrol sweeps.
forgotten-realms.place.caverns-of-the-cl.go_wrong: Trolls may menace the surrounding area.
forgotten-realms.place.caverns-of-the-cl.who_may: Trolls from the Stonelands lair there.
forgotten-realms.place.caverns-of-the-cl.where_from: Stonecliff, east of Eveningstar in Cormyr.

effect.summary: The cliff beside the High Road where the Caverns of the Claws are located.

forgotten-realms.place.high-road.name: High Road

effect.summary: Carries overland traffic and trade.

forgotten-realms.place.high-road.go_wrong: It was damaged and later rebuilt.
forgotten-realms.place.high-road.where_from: Near Neverwinter and along the Sword Coast.
forgotten-realms.place.high-road.combines: Its restoration resumed trade with Waterdeep and southern realms.

forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.name: Crumbling Stair

effect.summary: A broken marble stair and associated underways haunted by apparitions and dangerous traps.

forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.cost_or_limit: Cellars may collapse and may harbor beholders.
forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.go_wrong: Some apparitions lure intruders into deadly traps.
forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.where_from: Sword Hills east of Waterdeep, between Ardeep Forest and Uluvin.
forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.combines: The stair is held aloft by fading spells.
forgotten-realms.place.crumbling-stair.blocked_reason: The stair’s ongoing levitation is a persistent magical effect on a large structure.

effect.summary: A region east of Waterdeep containing the Crumbling Stair.
A settlement near the Crumbling Stair.

forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-wond.name: Crypt of the Wondermakers

effect.summary: A tavern cellar crypt said to hold undead magic-item makers and their collections.

forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-wond.go_wrong: Guardians and an eater of magic protect it.
forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-wond.combines: Contains helmed horrors, golems, automatons, and a nishruu in a stasis sphere.

forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.name: Dragonspear Castle

effect.summary: A ruined fortress repeatedly occupied by monsters and fiends arriving through a portal.

forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.cost_or_limit: The shrine and defenders face a continuing siege.
forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.go_wrong: The site repeatedly becomes a lair for hostile beings.
forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.who_may: Adventurers assisting the defenders are welcomed and may claim plunder.
forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.where_from: Trade Way south of Daggerford, past the High Moor.
forgotten-realms.place.dragonspear-castl.combines: A portal, Underdark connections, and a shrine of Tempus are present.

forgotten-realms.place.dread-lair-of-alo.name: Dread Lair of Alokkair

effect.summary: An ancient tomb connected to a chasm and said to hold great magic.

forgotten-realms.place.dread-lair-of-alo.cost_or_limit: The fate of Alokkair and the state of its treasure are uncertain.

forgotten-realms.place.fox-ridge.name: Fox Ridge

effect.summary: A forested, cave-riddled ridge containing the entrance to Alokkair’s lair.

forgotten-realms.place.fox-ridge.combines: A cave leads to an ancient tomb.

effect.summary: A legendary chasm beyond Alokkair’s tomb, said to lie near great magic.
A lost realm once ruled by Alokkair.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-cr.name: Dungeon of the Crypt

effect.summary: A dungeon below Waterdeep’s burial district, linked underground to Undermountain.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-cr.cost_or_limit: Its entrance has not been found since the Company of Crazed Venturers retired.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-cr.go_wrong: It contains vampires, nagas, and traps.

forgotten-realms.place.city-of-the-dead.name: City of the Dead

effect.summary: Waterdeep’s burial district, beneath which the Dungeon of the Crypt lies.

forgotten-realms.place.city-of-the-dead.combines: A secret stair from a crypt reaches the dungeon.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-death.name: Dungeon of Death

effect.summary: A dwarven gem mine later used by a troll king as a prison for human slaves.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-death.go_wrong: Imps and fiends have reportedly appeared nearby.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-death.where_from: Southern Lurkwood, Sword Coast North, near Shining Creek headwaters.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-death.combines: Built by the Deepdelve dwarven clan; later controlled by Glarauuth.

effect.summary: Cold, mysterious forest serving as home to goblinoid groups.
A creek whose headwaters are near the Dungeon of Death.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ha.name: Dungeon of the Hark

effect.summary: A subterranean stronghold used by brigands, including wererats and a bandit leader called the Hark.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ha.where_from: Northern edge of the High Moor.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ru.name: Dungeon of the Ruins

effect.summary: A monster-infested dungeon beneath the ruins of a former wizardry school and dwarf hold.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ru.cost_or_limit: It remains unexplored and may hold the lost Company of the Riven Orb’s bones.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ru.go_wrong: Monsters and strange frog-like beings are reported there.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ru.where_from: Near Settlestone, north of the Rauvin-Surbrin confluence.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-the-ru.combines: The dungeon predates the school and was once a dwarf hold.

forgotten-realms.place.rivers-rauvin-and.name: Rivers Rauvin and Surbrin

effect.summary: Their confluence is a geographic landmark near the Dungeon of the Ruins.

forgotten-realms.place.rivers-rauvin-and.combines: The dungeon lies north of their meeting point.

forgotten-realms.place.settlestone.name: Settlestone

effect.summary: A nearby settlement founded to buffer the market for Mithral Hall’s ore.

forgotten-realms.place.settlestone.who_may: Dwarves of Clan Ironshield founded it.
forgotten-realms.place.settlestone.combines: A garrison guards the approach to Mithral Hall.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-swords.name: Dungeon of Swords

effect.summary: An abandoned gnome mine occupied by monsters and guarded by animated flying magic swords.

forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-swords.cost_or_limit: Its depths reportedly hold a one-way portal north.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-swords.where_from: Serpent Hills east of the High Moor.
forgotten-realms.place.dungeon-of-swords.combines: The Cult of the Dragon found the mine monster-infested.

forgotten-realms.place.evermoors.name: Evermoors

effect.summary: The northern destination of the one-way portal said to lie in Dungeon of Swords.

forgotten-realms.place.evermoors.combines: Connected to Dungeon of Swords by a portal.

forgotten-realms.place.endless-caverns.name: Endless Caverns

effect.summary: A sprawling cavern system in the High Forest that ultimately connects to the Underdark.

forgotten-realms.place.endless-caverns.cost_or_limit: It extends for many miles underground.
forgotten-realms.place.endless-caverns.go_wrong: It has housed dragons and slaver bands.
forgotten-realms.place.endless-caverns.where_from: South of the Star Mounts in the High Forest.
forgotten-realms.place.endless-caverns.combines: Includes natural caves and deliberately cut passages.

forgotten-realms.place.fell-pass.name: Fell Pass

effect.summary: A pass haunted by an orc horde’s ghosts and containing a buried dwarven stronghold.

forgotten-realms.place.fell-pass.cost_or_limit: The chambers are said to be infested by beholders and gargoyles.
forgotten-realms.place.fell-pass.go_wrong: The old battle remains as a haunting.
forgotten-realms.place.fell-pass.where_from: Sword Coast North, between Mount Arinratha and Mount Thalangabold.
forgotten-realms.place.fell-pass.combines: The underground stronghold enabled dwarven warriors to attack from all sides.

forgotten-realms.place.mount-arinratha.name: Mount Arinratha

effect.summary: A mountain bordering Fell Pass.

forgotten-realms.place.mount-arinratha.combines: Fell Pass lies between it and Mount Thalangabold.

forgotten-realms.place.mount-thalangabol.name: Mount Thalangabold

effect.summary: A mountain bordering Fell Pass.

forgotten-realms.place.mount-thalangabol.combines: Fell Pass lies between it and Mount Arinratha.

forgotten-realms.place.gauntlgrym.name: Gauntlgrym

effect.summary: A large ancient dwarven city beneath the Crags, now infested by monsters.

forgotten-realms.place.gauntlgrym.cost_or_limit: Its lowest cellars lead into the Underdark.
forgotten-realms.place.gauntlgrym.go_wrong: Monsters, including mind flayers and ghosts, occupy it.
forgotten-realms.place.gauntlgrym.where_from: Under the Crags south of Mirabar, Sword Coast North.
forgotten-realms.place.gauntlgrym.combines: A former red dragon laired in its ventilation shaft; deepspawn produce monsters for its current inhabitants.

effect.summary: A region beneath which Gauntlgrym is located.

forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-four-gho.name: Halls of Four Ghosts

effect.summary: A ruined dwarf hall haunted by four ghosts and linked to a subterranean stronghold.

forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-four-gho.cost_or_limit: The underground network extends through miles of tunnels.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-four-gho.go_wrong: The tunnels contain trolls and routes used by slavers.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-four-gho.where_from: Western edge of the High Forest, Sword Coast North.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-four-gho.combines: A dry well shaft opens into the underground stronghold.

forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.name: Halls of the Hammer

effect.summary: A quarry, dwarf hold, and abandoned lodge associated with a glowing animated warhammer.

forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.cost_or_limit: Exploring it has repeatedly proved fatal.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.go_wrong: The central chamber may contain many hanging corpses or be empty.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.who_may: The hammer reportedly refuses to leave the hold.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.where_from: Northeastern High Moor, east of Highstar Lake.
forgotten-realms.place.halls-of-the-hamm.combines: Helmed horrors and watchghosts are present.

effect.summary: A lake east of which the Halls of the Hammer are located.

forgotten-realms.place.haunted-halls-of-.name: Haunted Halls of Eveningstar

effect.summary: A former bandit hold and later monster lair, now used for storage and explored by adventurers.

forgotten-realms.place.haunted-halls-of-.cost_or_limit: The location remains monster-infested and haunted.
forgotten-realms.place.haunted-halls-of-.go_wrong: Violent deaths have produced hauntings; monsters and wizards have fought there.
forgotten-realms.place.haunted-halls-of-.who_may: Adventurers and thrill-seekers visit; the local temple offers guides.
forgotten-realms.place.haunted-halls-of-.where_from: Starwater Gorge, near Eveningstar in northern Cormyr.

forgotten-realms.place.starwater-gorge.name: Starwater Gorge

effect.summary: A gorge whose western wall contains the Haunted Halls.

forgotten-realms.place.starwater-gorge.combines: The halls are cut into its rock wall.

forgotten-realms.place.eveningstar.name: Eveningstar

effect.summary: A farming village near the Haunted Halls and several other sites.

forgotten-realms.place.eveningstar.combines: The halls lie just north of it.

forgotten-realms.place.heroes-tomb.name: Heroes’ Tomb

effect.summary: A dwarf-built crypt beneath the ruins of Thruldar, repeatedly searched for another legendary crypt.

forgotten-realms.place.heroes-tomb.go_wrong: Exploration may expose adventurers to monsters.
forgotten-realms.place.heroes-tomb.where_from: Eastern end of the Lluirwood, north of Luiren.
forgotten-realms.place.heroes-tomb.combines: Said to lie above the Crypt of the Magicians.

forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-magi.name: Crypt of the Magicians

effect.summary: A crypt said to hold dead archwizards’ bones and magic somewhere beneath Thruldar.

forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-magi.cost_or_limit: Its location has not been found.
forgotten-realms.place.crypt-of-the-magi.combines: Said to be below the Heroes’ Tomb.

forgotten-realms.place.hidden-house.name: Hidden House

effect.summary: Its walls and passages change, and doors may open into different rooms from one visit to the next.

forgotten-realms.place.hidden-house.combines: Its rooms are linked by changing passages.

forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.name: Holdfast

forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.go_wrong: An undead human mage is reportedly trapped inside.
forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.who_may: Adventurers have fled it in disarray.
forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.where_from: Cormanthor, entered via the Standing Stone.
forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.combines: Portals link its rooms; magic traps and animated constructs guard it.
forgotten-realms.place.holdfast.blocked_reason: Portal-linked rooms and concealed access require spatial mechanics beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.place.house-of-stone.name: House of Stone

effect.summary: A huge maze-like tower built by dwarves and elves, containing chambers, phantoms, and monsters.

forgotten-realms.place.house-of-stone.go_wrong: Underdark creatures enter through its well.
forgotten-realms.place.house-of-stone.who_may: Outsiders were once kept away by moon elves.

effect.summary: The original name of the House of Stone.

forgotten-realms.place.stoneturn-well.name: Stoneturn Well

effect.summary: A well at the heart of the House of Stone, fed by an Underdark lake.

forgotten-realms.place.stoneturn-well.go_wrong: Monsters rise through it into the tower.

forgotten-realms.place.asmaeringlol.name: Asmaeringlol

effect.summary: A deep underground lake, also called Giantgout, that feeds Stoneturn Well.

forgotten-realms.place.asmaeringlol.go_wrong: Monsters travel upward from it through the well.
forgotten-realms.place.asmaeringlol.where_from: Underdark beneath the House of Stone.

forgotten-realms.place.ironguard.name: Ironguard

effect.summary: A small rock-cut tomb, dwelling, and guard shelter protected by animated flying daggers.

forgotten-realms.place.ironguard.combines: Its guardians resemble those in Undermountain.

forgotten-realms.place.lonely-tower.name: Lonely Tower

effect.summary: A tall tower said to house a wizard and guarded by orcs and elementals.

forgotten-realms.place.lonely-tower.cost_or_limit: Its current owner wants no visitors.
forgotten-realms.place.lonely-tower.go_wrong: The tower has numerous cellars and potentially dangerous inhabitants.
forgotten-realms.place.lonely-tower.where_from: West of the Cold Wood, northern Sword Coast North.
forgotten-realms.place.lonely-tower.combines: A cellar contains a sentient-seeming glowing healing pool.

effect.summary: A forest east of the Lonely Tower.

forgotten-realms.place.lyrar-s-hold.name: Lyrar’s Hold

effect.summary: A former hold whose keep has vanished, leaving underground storage caverns and passages.

forgotten-realms.place.lyrar-s-hold.combines: Dragons fought over its former keep as a lair site.

effect.summary: The location above the hidden ancient sarrukh city.
The lost tomb of Martek, Grand Vizier of Raurin.
A desert region containing the lost tomb of Martek.

forgotten-realms.place.mages-regal.name: Mages-Regal

effect.summary: A small cabal sought to control realms through selective killings, influence, illusions, and rumor.

forgotten-realms.place.mages-regal.cost_or_limit: They were few and engaged in feuds and battles.

forgotten-realms.place.mages-regal.where_from: Faerûn; associated with the Haunted Halls.

forgotten-realms.place.mages-regal.blocked_reason: The claimed mind-controlled pawns require mind-binding, beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.place.mussum.name: Mussum

effect.summary: A Chondathan settlement left abandoned after a devastating plague.

forgotten-realms.place.mussum.blocked_reason: It is a geographic location, not a game effect.

forgotten-realms.place.myth-rhynn.name: Myth Rhynn

effect.summary: Its mythal once prevented undead animation and repelled dragons; now decayed magic corrupts the surrounding forest.

forgotten-realms.place.myth-rhynn.go_wrong: The decayed mythal corrupts the forest.
forgotten-realms.place.myth-rhynn.combines: A mythal; undead prevention and dragon warding
forgotten-realms.place.myth-rhynn.blocked_reason: The mythal affects broad areas and multiple categories of beings and magic.

forgotten-realms.place.nameless-dungeon.name: Nameless Dungeon

effect.summary: A ruin containing a crypt and a separate underground storage complex.

forgotten-realms.place.nameless-dungeon.combines: Fallen Eaerlann mansion, crypt, and storage complex

forgotten-realms.place.purple-halls.name: Purple Halls

effect.summary: Portals link two identical underground strongholds.

forgotten-realms.place.purple-halls.go_wrong: The Tethyrian site became monster-infested after its mercenary occupants died.
forgotten-realms.place.purple-halls.where_from: One site is in Tethyr; its twin is in the Spiderhaunt Peaks

forgotten-realms.place.sarbreen.name: Sarbreen

effect.summary: A flooded, ruined dwarven city beneath present-day Ravens Bluff.

forgotten-realms.place.sarbreen.combines: Forms much of the city's sewers; secret passages descend below it

forgotten-realms.place.shoonach.name: Shoonach

effect.summary: A mythal-like effect traps undead, strengthens fire magic, weakens cold magic, slows projectiles, and cancels divine necromancy.

forgotten-realms.place.shoonach.combines: Multiple magical effects; undead cannot escape

forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt.name: Southkrypt

effect.summary: An abandoned dwarven hold and former mine with a once-productive farm.

forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt.cost_or_limit: The farm has grown wild and tangled.
forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt.go_wrong: The hold is maze-like and occupied by many monsters.
forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt.where_from: Southern Sword Mountains, north of Kryptgarden Forest

forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt-garden.name: Southkrypt Garden

effect.summary: An alternate name for Southkrypt, recalling its dwarven farm.

forgotten-realms.place.southkrypt-garden.go_wrong: The farm is now wild and tangled.

forgotten-realms.place.spellgard-saharel.name: Spellgard (Saharelgard)

effect.summary: A labyrinthine, mold-covered fortress now occupied by monsters.

forgotten-realms.place.spellgard-saharel.combines: Former home of lich Saharel; includes a temple

forgotten-realms.place.temple-of-the-spl.name: Temple of the Splendor of Splendors

effect.summary: An underground temple repeatedly occupied by monsters and once used by a thieves' guild.

forgotten-realms.place.temple-of-the-spl.cost_or_limit: Its exact location is uncertain; the named gem may no longer be there.
forgotten-realms.place.temple-of-the-spl.go_wrong: Many adventuring parties have met their doom there.
forgotten-realms.place.temple-of-the-spl.combines: Associated with the Splendor of Splendors gem

forgotten-realms.place.tomb-of-the-archm.name: Tomb of the Archmage

effect.summary: A magic-rich tomb protected by traps and guardians.

forgotten-realms.place.tomb-of-the-archm.cost_or_limit: The tomb remains thought to be undisturbed.
forgotten-realms.place.tomb-of-the-archm.go_wrong: Its release of undead devastated a Zhentarim force.
forgotten-realms.place.tomb-of-the-archm.where_from: Northeastern Mountains of Tethyamar, near the River Tesh headwaters
forgotten-realms.place.tomb-of-the-archm.combines: Wyvern lair cavern, magical traps, guardians, and undead

forgotten-realms.place.warlock-s-crypt.name: Warlock’s Crypt

effect.summary: Larloch's lair, guarded by undead and spellwebs.

forgotten-realms.place.warlock-s-crypt.cost_or_limit: Approaching it provokes attacks by liches and magical fields.
forgotten-realms.place.warlock-s-crypt.go_wrong: Intruders may be destroyed or driven away.

forgotten-realms.place.warriors-crypt.name: Warriors’ Crypt

effect.summary: A plundered tomb now used as a Zhentarim cache and refuge.

forgotten-realms.place.warriors-crypt.go_wrong: Guarded by gargoyles and animated constructs.

forgotten-realms.place.whisper-s-crypt.name: Whisper’s Crypt

effect.summary: A former Zhentarim caravan way station containing rooms and spellbooks.

forgotten-realms.place.whisper-s-crypt.where_from: Connected to the Haunted Halls in the Stonelands

forgotten-realms.place.the-dales.name: The Dales

effect.summary: A settled region suited to adventures among ruins, forests, and nearby conflicts.

forgotten-realms.place.the-dales.combines: Nearby Cormanthor, Cormyr, Sembia, Moonsea, and the Vast

forgotten-realms.place.moonshae-isles.name: Moonshae Isles

effect.summary: Islands unified under Cymrych Hugh and later divided among kingdoms.

forgotten-realms.place.moonshae-isles.go_wrong: The kingdoms split after the High King dies without an heir.
forgotten-realms.place.moonshae-isles.blocked_reason: No special game capability is described.

effect.summary: A mining settlement sponsored by the Zhentarim.

forgotten-realms.place.green-bones.name: Green Bones

effect.summary: The lair site explored in an adventure about Azurphax.

forgotten-realms.place.green-bones.cost_or_limit: Designed for four characters around level 16.

effect.summary: Caves are sometimes used to watch the surrounding area.
Varlae’s residence.

forgotten-realms.place.complex-tanglefoo.name: COMPLEX TANGLEFOOT TRAP

effect.summary: A trapped passage leading toward the large chamber.

forgotten-realms.institution.the-chill.who_may: Goblinoids banded together as a tribe.
forgotten-realms.institution.the-chill.combines: Sometimes hired to fight threats including Uthgardt, orcs, and trolls.

forgotten-realms.institution.silent-rain.name: Silent Rain

effect.summary: An elven company that accepts jobs advancing elven causes or destroying threats such as orcs and gnolls.

forgotten-realms.institution.silent-rain.cost_or_limit: Employers must leave written notice in Elvish near Evereska; the company responds only if interested.

forgotten-realms.institution.the-bloodax.name: The Bloodaxes

effect.summary: A mercenary company founded by dwarven exiles and later opened to other outcasts.

forgotten-realms.institution.the-bloodax.cost_or_limit: Members are exiles, criminals, or misfits.
forgotten-realms.institution.the-bloodax.who_may: Outcasts seeking a fresh start and new family.

forgotten-realms.institution.wizards-of-.name: Wizards of High Sorcery

effect.summary: Order whose members are patrons of the gods of magic.

forgotten-realms.institution.wizards-of-.who_may: Spellcasters who revere their order’s deity.
forgotten-realms.institution.wizards-of-.combines: Spellcasters pursue arcane magic rather than divine power.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of Solamnia

effect.summary: Order for which the Purple Dragon Knight is a suitable model.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Knight of the Rose leadership is modeled by Purple Dragon Knight.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of the Rose

effect.summary: Leaders within the Knights of Solamnia who guide other knights.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Associated with the Purple Dragon Knight option.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of the Sword

effect.summary: Order whose members swear fealty and combine spellcasting with martial skill.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Associated with the Oath of the Crown.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of the Skull

effect.summary: Order whose members swear fealty and combine spellcasting with martial skill.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Associated with the Oath of the Crown.

effect.summary: Religious group whose deity Aureon is associated with the Arcana Domain.
Religious group associated with Shadow.

forgotten-realms.institution.blood-of-vo.name: Blood of Vol

effect.summary: Cult whose clerics may take the Arcana Domain.

forgotten-realms.institution.blood-of-vo.combines: Clerics may choose the Arcana Domain.

forgotten-realms.institution.silver-flam.name: Silver Flame

effect.summary: Faith whose monks may take the Sun Soul path.

forgotten-realms.institution.silver-flam.combines: Associated with the Way of the Sun Soul.

forgotten-realms.institution.house-lyran.name: House Lyrandar

effect.summary: House whose dragonmark can empower storm sorcerers.

forgotten-realms.institution.house-lyran.combines: Storm sorcerers use its dragonmark to guide ships.

forgotten-realms.institution.arcane-cong.name: Arcane Congress

effect.summary: Aundair organization whose agents include bladesingers.

forgotten-realms.institution.arcane-cong.combines: Agents protect its secrets and investigate magical threats.

forgotten-realms.institution.slave-lords.name: Slave Lords

effect.summary: Cabal that raids seaside communities and enslaves prisoners.

forgotten-realms.institution.slave-lords.combines: May train prisoners with martial aptitude as pit fighters.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of the Watch

effect.summary: Disciplined knights guarding several lands against Baklunish incursions.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.cost_or_limit: Maintain a near-monastic life and study battle tactics.
forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.where_from: Bissel, Gran March, Geoff, and Keoland.
forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Associated with the Purple Dragon Knight model.

forgotten-realms.institution.scarlet-bro.name: Scarlet Brotherhood

effect.summary: Sinister monastic organization with expertise in unarmed fighting and assassination.

forgotten-realms.institution.scarlet-bro.combines: Teaches the Way of the Long Death.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.name: Knights of the Hart

effect.summary: Faction suited to paladins taking the Oath of the Crown.

forgotten-realms.institution.knights-of-.combines: Associated with the Oath of the Crown.

forgotten-realms.institution.thieves-gui.name: thieves’ guild

effect.summary: Guild with influence across the world and extensive power in Greyhawk.

forgotten-realms.institution.thieves-gui.combines: The Mastermind can represent one of its ambitious members.

forgotten-realms.institution.costers.name: Costers

effect.summary: Alliance of small independent traders who share caravans and sell caravan space.

forgotten-realms.institution.costers.cost_or_limit: Caravan guards are paid 1 to 20 gp per level per day.

forgotten-realms.institution.dalemeet.name: Dalemeet

effect.summary: none

forgotten-realms.institution.dalemeet.cost_or_limit: Meets infrequently for four or five days

forgotten-realms.institution.council-of-.name: Council of Seven Burghers

effect.summary: none

forgotten-realms.institution.council-of-.who_may: Seven wealthiest folk of the dale

forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.name: Thunder Blessing

effect.summary: A divine blessing in 1306 DR increased the dwarven birthrate, with many twin births.

forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.cost_or_limit: The resulting birthrate is described as about half that of a young human land; nearly a fifth of post-blessing births are twins.
forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.mind: Some younger dwarves are less fearful of arcane magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.where_from: Moradin is credited with bestowing it.
forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.combines: Also called the Forge or the Thunder Blessing.
forgotten-realms.rule.thunder-blessing.blocked_reason: The rule describes a lasting change in dwarven births.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-2.name: Level Adjustment +2

effect.summary: Duergar are more powerful and gain levels more slowly than most common races.

forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-2.combines: Applies to advancement and character power.
forgotten-realms.rule.level-adjustment-2.blocked_reason: This is a stated character-progression limit.

forgotten-realms.rule.spell-like-abiliti.name: Spell-Like Abilities

effect.summary: Duergar can enlarge themselves and become invisible once per day.

forgotten-realms.rule.spell-like-abiliti.cost_or_limit: Each ability is usable once per day; it affects only the duergar and carried items; caster level is twice character level, minimum third.
forgotten-realms.rule.spell-like-abiliti.combines: Enlarge and invisibility are separate abilities.
forgotten-realms.rule.spell-like-abiliti.blocked_reason: The passage gives use limits but relies on unprovided spell rules for the precise effects.

forgotten-realms.rule.drow-sign-language.name: Drow Sign Language

effect.summary: Drow can communicate silently with visible hand gestures within 120 feet.

forgotten-realms.rule.drow-sign-language.cost_or_limit: Users must see one another; it has no alphabet or written form.
forgotten-realms.rule.drow-sign-language.who_may: Drow know it as a bonus language; others must spend skill points to learn it.
forgotten-realms.rule.drow-sign-language.blocked_reason: The stated communication limit can be represented directly.

forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsider.name: Native Outsider

effect.summary: Planetouched count as native outsiders, changing which effects can target them and how resurrection works.

forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsider.cost_or_limit: Humanoid-only effects do not affect them; extraplanar-targeting effects may; native-plane banishment does not send them away; they can be raised or resurrected normally.
forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsider.where_from: Their long residence makes Toril their native plane.
forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsider.combines: Alters interactions with humanoid and outsider effects and death recovery.
forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsider.blocked_reason: The resurrection distinction depends on representing the creature’s native-plane and death-recovery state.

forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-d.name: Patron deity and divine powers

effect.summary: A person needs a patron deity to gain divine powers and cannot have more than one patron at once.

forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-d.cost_or_limit: Changing patron is possible; some class combinations require an acceptable deity.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-d.who_may: People seeking divine powers or deity-dependent class levels
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-d.combines: Class requirements can restrict multiclassing unless the prior deity is acceptable or abandoned.
forgotten-realms.rule.patron-deity-and-d.blocked_reason: This is a rule of access and affiliation, not an unsupported supernatural effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.monk-multiclass-re.name: Monk multiclass restrictions

effect.summary: Order-specific approved multiclass paths can preserve monk advancement; violating restrictions ends it.

forgotten-realms.rule.monk-multiclass-re.cost_or_limit: Each order specifies permitted classes and may add level-balance limits.
forgotten-realms.rule.monk-multiclass-re.go_wrong: Taking an unapproved class or violating an order’s conditions prevents further monk advancement.
forgotten-realms.rule.monk-multiclass-re.combines: Overrides the usual ex-monk restriction where specified.

forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.name: Mage Runes and the Curse of Mystra

effect.summary: Arcane casters have personal identifying sigils; deceitful copying can trigger Mystra’s curse against the copier.

forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.cost_or_limit: Only powerful casters above 10th level receive the stated protection; the copier must make three DC 15 Will saves.
forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.go_wrong: Failed saves cause successive permanent Strength, Intelligence, and Wisdom drain; the second also causes feeblemind, and the third removes high-ability bonus spell slots for a month.
forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.who_may: All arcane spellcasters have sigils; Mystra protects powerful casters from deceitful misuse.
forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.where_from: Faerûnian arcane practice and Mystra’s protection
forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.combines: The curse escalates across three saves.
forgotten-realms.rule.mage-runes-and-the.blocked_reason: The escalating multi-save curse and lasting ability loss require a specific backlash and duration system.

forgotten-realms.rule.faer-nian-height-a.name: Faerûnian height and weight adjustments

effect.summary: Adjusts height or weight by ancestry and elemental nature.

forgotten-realms.rule.faer-nian-height-a.who_may: Elves, half-elves, drow, gray dwarves, aasimar, tieflings, and genasi use the stated adjustments.
forgotten-realms.rule.faer-nian-height-a.combines: Uses Player’s Handbook height and weight entries as its baseline.
forgotten-realms.rule.faer-nian-height-a.blocked_reason: The rule alters body measurements, a form change beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.prestige-class-cas.name: Prestige-class caster-level advancement

effect.summary: Some prestige levels that advance daily spells also increase caster level.

forgotten-realms.rule.prestige-class-cas.cost_or_limit: Applies to prestige classes that add to the base class for spells per day.
forgotten-realms.rule.prestige-class-cas.who_may: Characters with qualifying spellcasting prestige levels.
forgotten-realms.rule.prestige-class-cas.combines: Caster level is used for dispel checks and overcoming spell resistance.
forgotten-realms.rule.prestige-class-cas.blocked_reason: This progression rule can be represented as a lasting alteration to spellcasting.

forgotten-realms.rule.harper-scout-loss-.name: Harper scout loss and restoration of standing

effect.summary: Misconduct halts class advancement and disables three Harper gifts until formal restoration.

forgotten-realms.rule.harper-scout-loss-.cost_or_limit: Restoration requires a petition, a High Harper-assigned quest, and an atonement spell.
forgotten-realms.rule.harper-scout-loss-.who_may: Harper scouts who violate the code, endanger Harpers, or leave the society.
forgotten-realms.rule.harper-scout-loss-.combines: Restored standing allows future class advancement and restores the affected abilities.
forgotten-realms.rule.harper-scout-loss-.blocked_reason: The stated rule removes and restores abilities under explicit conditions.

forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.name: Wild magic zone spell check

effect.summary: Magic originating inside a wild magic zone must pass a caster-level check or face a random listed outcome.

forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.cost_or_limit: Check DC is 15 plus spell level; magic originating outside the zone and entering it is unaffected.
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.go_wrong: Failure invokes a random wild-magic outcome, ranging from rebound or misdirection to failure, normal operation, or enhanced effect.
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.who_may: Applies to casters and magic items within the zone
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.combines: Covers spells and spell-like abilities, not supernatural, extraordinary, or natural abilities.
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic-zone-sp.blocked_reason: It requires a stochastic table of altered outcomes, including resource consumption and effect changes.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.name: The Weave

effect.summary: Magic is a process by which beings shape pervasive natural energies through the Weave.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.cost_or_limit: Different magical traditions are distinct routes to manipulating the same energies.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.go_wrong: Powerful magic can damage the Weave.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.who_may: Beings able to wield magic through innate, learned, musical, or divine means
forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.combines: Mystra is bound to and governs Toril's Weave.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-weave.blocked_reason: It describes a shared underlying power system and damage to that system.

forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.name: Mystra's decree

effect.summary: The most perilous ancient magic is barred to mortals under Mystra's guardianship.

forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.cost_or_limit: Restriction persists until the world changes or divine powers relinquish their guardianship.
forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.who_may: Applies to mortals and dangerous magic
forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.where_from: Mystra's protection of the Weave after Karsus's attempted seizure of divinity
forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.combines: Aims to prevent further damage to the Weave.
forgotten-realms.rule.mystra-s-decree.blocked_reason: It restricts access to powerful magic through an external guardianship rule.

forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.name: Shadow Weave item effects

effect.summary: Shadow Weave items adjust spell effects by school and forbid light-designated effects.

forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.cost_or_limit: Enchantment, illusion, necromancy, and darkness gain bonuses; evocation and transmutation lose caster level and save DC.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.combines: Shadow Weave items and their generated effects.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.blocked_reason: The rules modify the strength and eligibility of other powers according to their school and designator.

forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.name: Shadow Weave item Wisdom damage

effect.summary: Item activation damages the user's Wisdom.

forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.cost_or_limit: Spell completion, trigger, or command-word activation deals 1d4 temporary Wisdom damage; use-activated items deal 1 point on first daily use; continuous items cause it at dusk or when put aside.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.go_wrong: Wisdom damage is the stated harmful consequence.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.mind: Temporary Wisdom damage unless the user has Shadow Weave Magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.combines: Shadow Weave Magic feat prevents the damage.
forgotten-realms.rule.shadow-weave-item-.blocked_reason: The cost can be represented as a direct mind effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.name: Rune capacity and triggering

effect.summary: Runes persist until triggered and are activated by touch.

forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.cost_or_limit: A Medium or smaller object holds one rune; larger objects hold one per 25 square feet; creatures cannot bear runes. A rune triggers once and is expended.
forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.go_wrong: Erasure, dispelling, or failed inscription can prevent its use.
forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.who_may: Whoever touches it triggers it, except its creator may touch it safely.
forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.combines: The stored spell affects the rune's triggerer; object-only spells require an object trigger.
forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.mechanism: stored power with trigger and capacity limit
forgotten-realms.rule.rune-capacity-and-.blocked_reason: The rule specifies item-carried powers, capacity, triggers, and depletion.

forgotten-realms.rule.portal-passage.name: Portal passage

effect.summary: Portals transport creatures but not unattended objects, and need adequate destination space.

forgotten-realms.rule.portal-passage.cost_or_limit: The destination must support the user and provide room; objects cannot pass unattended, while carried objects can.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-passage.go_wrong: An occupied destination redirects the user to a nearby suitable space; a blocked or unsafe destination can foil transport.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-passage.combines: A portal's direction and destinations determine travel.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-passage.blocked_reason: The rule governs relocation and destination occupancy.

forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.name: Portal malfunction

effect.summary: A malfunctioning portal can fail, drain magic, repel users, emit energy, misdirect travel, or work normally.

forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.cost_or_limit: Each activation rolls on the malfunction table; continuous portals apply the result for 1d10 rounds.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.go_wrong: Possible outcomes include dispelling effects, item depletion, damage, energy, or wrong destination.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.combines: Some results affect the user's items or magical effects.
forgotten-realms.rule.portal-malfunction.blocked_reason: The rule has multiple random failure outcomes, including damage and depletion.

forgotten-realms.rule.coin-metal-determi.name: Coin metal determines ordinary coin value
forgotten-realms.rule.coin-metal-determi.cost_or_limit: Coins are generally valued by their metal, except for locally supported tokens.

forgotten-realms.rule.coinage-conversion.name: Coinage conversion standard
forgotten-realms.rule.coinage-conversion.cost_or_limit: Ten copper pieces equal one silver, ten silver equal one gold, and ten gold equal one platinum.

forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-valuatio.name: Trade bar valuation
forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-valuatio.cost_or_limit: A one-pound silver bar is worth 5 gp and a one-pound gold bar 50 gp; heavier bars scale proportionally.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.name: Smokepowder and antimagic

effect.summary: Smokepowder does not function in antimagic fields or dead-magic areas.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.cost_or_limit: Restricted by antimagic or dead-magic zones.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.go_wrong: Its operation fails in those zones.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-and-an.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar lacks a field that disables an item’s operation.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.name: Smokepowder manufacture

effect.summary: Making smokepowder requires a specified feat and alchemical skill, and yields a fixed quantity.

forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.cost_or_limit: Craft Wondrous Item and Alchemy 9 ranks produce one pound worth 16 gp; one ounce fires a bullet.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.who_may: A creator meeting the stated prerequisites.
forgotten-realms.rule.smokepowder-manufa.blocked_reason: This rule concerns crafting prerequisites and consumable ammunition rather than a basic effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.name: Chultan material quality

effect.summary: Weapons made from inferior local materials take penalties to attacks and damage.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.cost_or_limit: A -2 penalty applies, with damage remaining at least 1.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.who_may: Characters using weapons made from inferior materials.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.combines: Materials include stone, wood, obsidian, or copper.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-material-q.blocked_reason: A numerical attack and damage modifier is directly usable.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.name: Chultan armor fatigue

effect.summary: Wearing sufficiently burdensome armor in the heat causes fatigue after an hour.

forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.cost_or_limit: Applies to armor with check penalty -5 or worse after one hour; fatigue lasts while worn and one further hour.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.go_wrong: Fatigue imposes -2 Strength and Dexterity and prevents running or charging.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.who_may: Characters wearing the specified armor in Chult.
forgotten-realms.rule.chultan-armor-fati.blocked_reason: The timed fatigue condition and penalties are directly representable.

forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.name: Purple Dragon’s fate and Cormyr

effect.summary: Some believe Cormyr will fall when the last Purple Dragon dies.

forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.cost_or_limit: The claim is presented as belief, not confirmed certainty.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.go_wrong: The kingdom may perish if the belief is true.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.who_may: Applies to Cormyr and the Purple Dragon.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.combines: The dragon’s death is linked to the kingdom’s fate.
forgotten-realms.rule.purple-dragon-s-fa.blocked_reason: A conditional world consequence can be represented as a rule.

effect.summary: An old agreement between the elves and the Dalesfolk.
A plot lead rather than a world mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.name: Deepingdale salmon restriction

effect.summary: Outsiders taking more than one salmon for a meal are treated as bandits.

forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.cost_or_limit: One salmon per outsider for a meal.
forgotten-realms.rule.deepingdale-salmon.go_wrong: Taking more brings a bandit accusation.

forgotten-realms.rule.four-dolphins-foun.name: Four Dolphins Fountain’s ward

effect.summary: Prevents scrying and eavesdropping magic from working in the courtyard.

forgotten-realms.rule.four-dolphins-foun.blocked_reason: The passage specifies a persistent area-wide magical suppression effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.name: Vauntagar creature cycle

effect.summary: Injured guarding monsters shift away and a fresh one takes their place.

forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.cost_or_limit: A cycle of monsters guards the pools
forgotten-realms.rule.vauntagar-creature.blocked_reason: The rule requires extradimensional creature storage and replacement.

forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.name: Lake of Steam volcanic warming

effect.summary: Underwater volcanic activity keeps the bay warm and produces steam and mist.

forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.go_wrong: Cold nights obscure the waters with dense mist
forgotten-realms.rule.lake-of-steam-volc.blocked_reason: The heat and mist can be represented with basic area effects.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.name: The Sisters’ welcome

effect.summary: Creatures of the Sisters allow deity-favored travelers to approach without challenge.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.cost_or_limit: Requires an invisible mark of nature-deity favor
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.go_wrong: Unfavored intruders may be warned of or opposed
forgotten-realms.rule.the-sisters-welcom.blocked_reason: The mark-based access restriction can be represented as a conditional rule.

forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.name: Dire Wood's outer-ring containment

effect.summary: Aberrations within the Dire Wood cannot cross its outer ring.

forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.combines: Magical chaos emanates from the central butte
forgotten-realms.rule.dire-wood-s-outer-.blocked_reason: A persistent boundary preventing creatures from crossing needs an area-field mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.name: Fountains of Memory transport

effect.summary: A being entering a pool to return to a past time instead teleports to a random place.

forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.who_may: A being entering a pool to reach the past
forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.combines: The pools also reflect images of the past
forgotten-realms.rule.fountains-of-memor.blocked_reason: Random relocation can be represented as a basic position-changing effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.name: The Memory of Steel

effect.summary: A magic weapon said to have lost powers in battle may regain them after immersion in a Fountain of Memory.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.cost_or_limit: Requires dipping the weapon into a Fountain of Memory
forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.who_may: A weapon owner able to reach a fountain
forgotten-realms.rule.the-memory-of-stee.blocked_reason: Restoring an item's lost powers requires a rule for powers embedded in items.

forgotten-realms.rule.stone-bridge-river.name: Stone Bridge river-binding

effect.summary: The bridge's magic holds the Dessarin River in place so it cannot change course.

forgotten-realms.rule.stone-bridge-river.cost_or_limit: The river remains fixed despite attempts to snake elsewhere

forgotten-realms.rule.veldorn-mutual-def.name: Veldorn mutual defense

forgotten-realms.rule.yuirwood-divinatio.name: Yuirwood divination concealment

forgotten-realms.rule.bhaal-water-curse.name: Bhaal water curse

forgotten-realms.rule.deity-power-rankin.name: Deity power ranking

forgotten-realms.rule.lolth-s-clerics-ar.name: Lolth’s clerics are always female

forgotten-realms.rule.mask-s-secret-tunn.name: Mask’s secret-tunnel temples

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shadow-weave.name: The Shadow Weave

forgotten-realms.rule.native-outsiders-a.name: Native outsiders are not warded from their home plane

forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.combines: Their former master’s destruction frees them
forgotten-realms.rule.wan-shades-reclaim.blocked_reason: Restoring identity and personal history to undead requires soul and memory-state mechanics.

forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.name: Dark Fissure planar rift

effect.summary: Portals to the Abyss open a massive rift that pulls constructs into otherness.

forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.cost_or_limit: Requires the drithdarkar to open portals.
forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.go_wrong: The rift removes the advancing constructs from the battlefield.
forgotten-realms.rule.dark-fissure-plana.blocked_reason: A large-scale rift affects an army over an area.

forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.name: Ninety-nine years of service for Eltab’s release

effect.summary: Myrkul’s followers agree to serve Eltab for ninety-nine years in return for releasing him.

forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.go_wrong: The bargain frees Eltab and enables his rise to power.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.who_may: The followers of Myrkul make the agreement.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.combines: Exchanges service for release from binding.
forgotten-realms.rule.ninety-nine-years-.blocked_reason: It requires a binding and release condition with a duration and exchange.

forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.name: Laws of Battle

effect.summary: Rules drafted to prevent a recurrence of genocidal slaughter like the battles against the merrow.

forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.cost_or_limit: Intended to constrain warfare and prevent mass slaughter.
forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.who_may: Drafted by merfolk, shalarins, and Dukars
forgotten-realms.rule.laws-of-battle.blocked_reason: The passage gives their purpose but no specific unsupported game effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.name: Myth Nantar's expanding mythal

effect.summary: Where the mythal reaches, it bars matter and magic except corals, sea stars, and fish.

forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.cost_or_limit: Its protection spreads gradually over the city.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.go_wrong: Touching it produces haunting singing and discourages nearby visitors.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.mind: The singing influences local beliefs about a curse.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.where_from: The mythal surrounding the Academy of the Dukars.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.combines: Exempts corals, sea stars, and fish.
forgotten-realms.rule.myth-nantar-s-expa.blocked_reason: Its gradual, area-wide selective barrier is more than a simple instantaneous block.

forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.name: Sacred Secrets

effect.summary: The location of the replaying door is kept secret by Azuth and Mystra.

forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.cost_or_limit: Access to the location is limited to the secret's holders.
forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.who_may: Azuth and Mystra share the secret.
forgotten-realms.rule.sacred-secrets.blocked_reason: The rule concerns concealment of information.

forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.name: Wulgreth's transformation into a lich

effect.summary: Unleashed magical energies transform Wulgreth into a lich.

forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.cost_or_limit: Occurs upon his death amid released magical energies.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.go_wrong: The event creates the Dire Wood as well.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.where_from: Magical energies released when he dies.
forgotten-realms.rule.wulgreth-s-transfo.blocked_reason: Changing a being into a lich is a substantial form transformation.

forgotten-realms.rule.wisdom-and-not-arm.name: wisdom and not armed might will rule in the city

effect.summary: Waterdeep’s rule is to rest on wisdom rather than military force.

forgotten-realms.rule.wisdom-and-not-arm.blocked_reason: This is a governance rule rather than a special game effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.name: Magic bowls’ duration and poison limitation

effect.summary: The bowls' clear-thought benefit lasts an hour and does not prevent poisoning.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.cost_or_limit: One hour of benefit; no poison protection
forgotten-realms.rule.magic-bowls-durati.blocked_reason: The duration and stated limitation can be tracked with ordinary effect duration and item rules.

forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.name: Enchanted collar distance restriction

effect.summary: The wearer cannot move farther than a set distance from the Master.

forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.cost_or_limit: Movement is limited by an unspecified radius
forgotten-realms.rule.enchanted-collar-d.blocked_reason: The restriction acts continuously on a bound person.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.name: The Time of Troubles

effect.summary: Gods are forced to walk the Realms as mortals while magic grows unreliable and prayers fail.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.cost_or_limit: The gods seek the Tablets of Fate to return to their domains
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.go_wrong: Magic becomes unpredictable and divine prayers go unanswered
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.where_from: Lord Ao casts the gods out of their domains
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.combines: The Tablets of Fate are the key to the gods’ return
forgotten-realms.rule.the-time-of-troubl.blocked_reason: The rule involves divine embodiment and return between planes, beyond the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.name: Godstrife’s awakening of Myth Rhynn

effect.summary: An awakening of evil in the ruins imbues nearby creatures with a drive to maraud together.

forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.go_wrong: Disparate creatures are compelled to act together despite their usual hostility
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.mind: Imposes a desire to maraud and despoil
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.combines: The creatures move in bands despite differing natures
forgotten-realms.rule.godstrife-s-awaken.blocked_reason: The rule imposes a lasting drive on creatures’ minds.

forgotten-realms.rule.death-and-rebirth-.name: Death and rebirth of Torm

effect.summary: Torm dies and is later reborn during the Time of Troubles.

forgotten-realms.rule.death-and-rebirth-.blocked_reason: Death and subsequent divine rebirth require a soul-state mechanic.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.name: The Shaking Plague

effect.summary: A contagious illness causes pallor and uncontrollable shaking; some recover after months, while severe cases die.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.cost_or_limit: Contagious for roughly ten days after onset; prior victims become less susceptible.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.go_wrong: Severe spasms can prevent breathing and cause death.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-shaking-plague.blocked_reason: The passage provides a gameable disease process and duration.

forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.name: Life-extending magic in the red gem

effect.summary: Akhlaur and Zalathorm owe their long lives to magic they made together; destroying its final gem-held portion kills them.

forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.cost_or_limit: The remaining power is housed in the gem.
forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.go_wrong: Destroying the gem ends their lives.
forgotten-realms.rule.life-extending-mag.blocked_reason: The passage establishes a power-bearing item and lethal loss but gives no operating or depletion rules.

forgotten-realms.rule.demons-beneath-dun.name: Demons beneath Dun-Tharos awaken

effect.summary: The struggle stirs previously dormant demons beneath the ruins.

forgotten-realms.rule.demons-beneath-dun.cost_or_limit: The struggle is the stated catalyst.

forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.name: Rage of Dragons ends

effect.summary: Ending the High Magic that caused the dragon rage ends the Rage.

forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.cost_or_limit: The rage is sustained by elven High Magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.go_wrong: Dragons were driven into a widespread rage.
forgotten-realms.rule.rage-of-dragons-en.combines: Its end releases Bahamut from an ancient prison.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.name: Dead raised as shadows

effect.summary: Volumvax raises the dead of Ordulin as shadows to strengthen his army.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.cost_or_limit: Requires Volumvax’s action; other limits are unstated.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.go_wrong: The dead become hostile army members.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.mind: Their new allegiance is not explained.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-raised-as-sha.blocked_reason: The transformation and continued state of the dead are not runnable with the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.name: Kiaransalee erased from the Realms

effect.summary: With her name and worshipers removed, the deity fades from existence.

forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.cost_or_limit: The account links the erasure to High Magic and loss of worshipers.
forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.who_may: Q’arlynd Melarn and apprentices perform the ritual.
forgotten-realms.rule.kiaransalee-erased.blocked_reason: The disappearance and cessation of a deity’s existence require a soul-state mechanism.

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.name: Elven High Magic causes dragon rage

effect.summary: A High Magic working causes dragons to enter a rage.

forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.cost_or_limit: The rage lasts until the working ends.
forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.combines: Ending the working ends the rage.
forgotten-realms.rule.elven-high-magic-c.blocked_reason: It affects dragons broadly across a region rather than a single target.

forgotten-realms.rule.coin-acceptance.name: Coin acceptance

effect.summary: Pure coins of standard weight are generally accepted at face value across Faerûn, but not every polity mints each type.

forgotten-realms.rule.coin-acceptance.cost_or_limit: Acceptance is not universal for every issuer or coin.

forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-standard.name: Trade bar standard

effect.summary: A commonly used five-pound silver bar has a standard size and is valued at 25 gp.

forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-standard.cost_or_limit: Applies to the common bar size and composition.
forgotten-realms.rule.trade-bar-standard.combines: Trade bars substitute for large piles of coins or gems.

effect.summary: A Torilian year has 365 days, divided into twelve 30-day months, three tendays per month, and five annual holidays.
Every four years, Shieldmeet adds a day after Midsummer.

forgotten-realms.rule.shifting-of-the-se.name: Shifting of the Seasons

effect.summary: The seasons began later and ended later after the celestial shift of 1487–1488 DR.

forgotten-realms.rule.shifting-of-the-se.cost_or_limit: The change affected seasonal timing; its duration is uncertain.

effect.summary: The year count in Toril’s history begins at 1 DR and spread across Faerûn.

forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.name: Gods’ mortal exile

effect.summary: In 1358 DR the gods were cast from their realm and incarnated as mortals.

forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.cost_or_limit: The gods sought to recover their divinity.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.go_wrong: They warred; some died, while some mortals ascended.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.who_may: Gods and a handful of mortals.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.combines: Magic became unpredictable and prayers went unanswered.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-mortal-exile.blocked_reason: Divine status and mortal ascension are not represented by the basic effect grammar.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-item-stored-.name: Magic-item stored effect

effect.summary: Item creation ties Weave threads into an object to hold an effect until its user calls it forth.

forgotten-realms.rule.magic-item-stored-.cost_or_limit: The effect lasts as long as the item does.
forgotten-realms.rule.magic-item-stored-.who_may: An item user need not be a spellcaster.
forgotten-realms.rule.magic-item-stored-.combines: An item’s effect may require attunement.
forgotten-realms.rule.magic-item-stored-.blocked_reason: The effect is stored in an item and released by its user, which requires item-carried power.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.name: Dead Magic

effect.summary: In rare areas without the Weave, spells, magic items, and some innate abilities stop working.

forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.go_wrong: Innate Weave-linked abilities can fail as their carried knot unravels.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.who_may: Affects spellcasters, items, and intrinsically magical creatures in the area.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.where_from: Areas where the Weave is absent.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.combines: Disables spells and magic items as well as some innate abilities.
forgotten-realms.rule.dead-magic.blocked_reason: The rule removes magical operation from a region and affects multiple categories of power.

forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic.name: Wild Magic

effect.summary: In a wild-magic area, the Weave forms spontaneous effects and twists spell results.

forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic.cost_or_limit: Occurs in areas of wild magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic.combines: Can create spontaneous magical constructs and distort spells.
forgotten-realms.rule.wild-magic.blocked_reason: The rule creates spontaneous and unpredictable changes to magical outcomes.

forgotten-realms.rule.divine-magic-depen.name: Divine magic depends on a god’s presence

effect.summary: When a god leaves a pantheon, its divine magic, associated miracles and omens cease.

forgotten-realms.rule.divine-magic-depen.cost_or_limit: A god’s withdrawal stops divine power reaching followers.
forgotten-realms.rule.divine-magic-depen.go_wrong: Faith and holy sites may be abandoned or taken over.

forgotten-realms.rule.gods-choose-divine.name: Gods choose divine spellcasters without a formula

effect.summary: The gods decide privately which mortals receive divine magical insight.

forgotten-realms.rule.gods-choose-divine.cost_or_limit: No predictable selection method is given.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-choose-divine.mind: Recipients have their minds and souls opened to magic.
forgotten-realms.rule.gods-choose-divine.who_may: Chosen mortals; some refuse or embrace the gift.

forgotten-realms.rule.tempus-s-honor.name: Tempus’s Honor

effect.summary: A code of warfare calls for arming the needy, respecting foes, acting bravely, training for battle, and avoiding feuds and atrocities.

forgotten-realms.rule.tempus-s-honor.cost_or_limit: Condemns poisoning wells, tainting fields, harming noncombatants, and torture.
forgotten-realms.rule.tempus-s-honor.who_may: Followers of Tempus are taught to observe it.
forgotten-realms.rule.tempus-s-honor.combines: Intended to make conflicts shorter and safer for those not fighting.

forgotten-realms.rule.souls-wait-on-the-.name: souls wait on the Fugue Plane

effect.summary: After death, souls wait until a deity claims them or Kelemvor judges their destination.

forgotten-realms.rule.souls-wait-on-the-.cost_or_limit: Those who fit no favored deity’s ethos may wait for centuries.
forgotten-realms.rule.souls-wait-on-the-.go_wrong: A soul may receive a devil’s offer of infernal power or comfort.
forgotten-realms.rule.souls-wait-on-the-.combines: Deities and devils may approach waiting souls.
forgotten-realms.rule.souls-wait-on-the-.blocked_reason: The rule depends on souls persisting after death and being assigned an afterlife.

forgotten-realms.rule.daggerford-militia.name: Daggerford militia service

effect.summary: Able-bodied adults serve the militia for twenty years and spend at least one day monthly on defense duty.

forgotten-realms.rule.daggerford-militia.cost_or_limit: Applies to able-bodied adults; residents receive weapons instruction.
forgotten-realms.rule.daggerford-militia.combines: Training includes spears and other weapons.

forgotten-realms.rule.karsus-s-failed-se.name: Karsus’s failed seizure of the Weave

effect.summary: Karsus’s attempt to take control of the Weave killed magic’s goddess, shattered the Weave, and caused stranded floating cities to crash.

forgotten-realms.rule.karsus-s-failed-se.cost_or_limit: The attempt nearly succeeded but failed catastrophically.
forgotten-realms.rule.karsus-s-failed-se.go_wrong: The goddess died, magic’s fabric was torn, and enclaves fell.
forgotten-realms.rule.karsus-s-failed-se.who_may: The attempt was made by the mage Karsus.
forgotten-realms.rule.karsus-s-failed-se.combines: Led to the collapse of Netherese flying enclaves.

forgotten-realms.rule.everbright-treatme.name: Everbright treatment

effect.summary: Treated metal keeps its shine and resists natural, and sometimes magical, pitting, rust, and tarnish.

forgotten-realms.rule.everbright-treatme.cost_or_limit: Works on armor, weapons, and other metal objects; results vary by maker.
forgotten-realms.rule.everbright-treatme.go_wrong: Other races imitate the process with uneven success.
forgotten-realms.rule.everbright-treatme.who_may: Dwarves discovered the technique; others have copied it.
forgotten-realms.rule.everbright-treatme.blocked_reason: The rule changes ongoing material qualities of treated objects rather than performing a basic instantaneous effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.silverymoon-mythal.name: Silverymoon mythal restrictions

effect.summary: Within the mythal, spells summoning flame, conjuring creatures, or permitting teleportation fail.

forgotten-realms.rule.silverymoon-mythal.cost_or_limit: Applies to those spell categories inside the field’s boundary.
forgotten-realms.rule.silverymoon-mythal.who_may: Anyone attempting the specified spells within the city.
forgotten-realms.rule.silverymoon-mythal.blocked_reason: The rule depends on an ongoing area field that selectively blocks spells.

forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-undergro.name: Waterdeep underground access law

effect.summary: Living or digging below Waterdeep’s surface is illegal unless the lords authorize it.

forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-undergro.go_wrong: Unauthorized residence or digging violates the law.
forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-undergro.who_may: People authorized by the lords may do so.
forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-undergro.combines: Applies to underground areas including the Warrens and Downshadow.
forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-undergro.blocked_reason: This is a legal restriction on who may occupy or excavate a defined area.

forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-burial-r.name: Waterdeep burial restriction

effect.summary: The dead may legally be buried only in the City of the Dead.

forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-burial-r.combines: The designated cemetery is the City of the Dead.
forgotten-realms.rule.waterdeep-burial-r.blocked_reason: The rule restricts a civic activity to a single designated location.

forgotten-realms.rule.adbar-mine-access.name: Adbar mine access

effect.summary: The mines are closed to visitors, including non-Adbarran dwarves, except in major emergencies.

forgotten-realms.rule.adbar-mine-access.cost_or_limit: Only great emergencies permit visitor access.
forgotten-realms.rule.adbar-mine-access.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward access restriction.

forgotten-realms.rule.thornhold-defense-.name: Thornhold defense secrecy

effect.summary: Only Stoneshaft elders know the complete plans for the fortress defenses.

forgotten-realms.rule.thornhold-defense-.cost_or_limit: Any one dwarf knows only part of the plan.
forgotten-realms.rule.thornhold-defense-.go_wrong: Captors could use torture or kidnapping to seek information.
forgotten-realms.rule.thornhold-defense-.who_may: The elders hold the complete knowledge.
forgotten-realms.rule.thornhold-defense-.blocked_reason: The rule can be represented as divided information access.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-elf-s-eye-arcs.name: The elf’s eye arcs guide them toward the afterlife

effect.summary: Arcs above an elderly elf’s pupils signal guidance toward the elven afterlife.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-elf-s-eye-arcs.cost_or_limit: Arcs can blind the elf to the world
forgotten-realms.rule.the-elf-s-eye-arcs.go_wrong: The elf loses sight of the present world
forgotten-realms.rule.the-elf-s-eye-arcs.combines: The arcs vanish upon entry to the next realm
forgotten-realms.rule.the-elf-s-eye-arcs.blocked_reason: It describes guidance into an afterlife and a change in the elf’s state of sight.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-star-ro.name: Evermeet’s star route

effect.summary: Travelers must follow one star pattern and then switch to a new one to find Evermeet.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-star-ro.cost_or_limit: The route changes during the voyage
forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-star-ro.blocked_reason: The passage describes a navigation procedure rather than a supernatural effect.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-magic-s.name: Evermeet’s magic soothes the body and conscience

effect.summary: The island’s magic can ease physical aches and guilty feelings.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-magic-s.blocked_reason: The described effect is attributed to the island’s pervasive magic, without a limited target or range.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-first-sunderin.name: The first Sundering

effect.summary: High Mages brought Toril into contact with Arvandor, causing calamity.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-first-sunderin.cost_or_limit: The passage gives no further mechanism
forgotten-realms.rule.the-first-sunderin.combines: Its echo is said to recur in later calamities
forgotten-realms.rule.the-first-sunderin.blocked_reason: The rule describes a world-scale planar connection and resulting calamity.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-three-p.name: Evermeet’s three-plane existence

effect.summary: Evermeet touches Toril, the Feywild, and Arvandor while fully existing in none.

forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-three-p.cost_or_limit: Finding it requires following the changing stars
forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-three-p.go_wrong: Straying from its route leads to loss
forgotten-realms.rule.evermeet-s-three-p.blocked_reason: The described condition places one island across multiple planes simultaneously.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.name: The Creed Resolute

effect.summary: Its sworn rules forbid assigning the Companion to one god and require service to the High Observer, Elturgard’s laws, and the greater good.

forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.cost_or_limit: Applies to those who swear the oaths; members may be reminded to correct misconduct.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.mind: Creates a lasting commitment to the oath’s principles.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.who_may: Companions and Hellriders who take the oath
forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.where_from: Created by Elturgard’s first High Observer
forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.combines: Used to unite the Companions and later adopted by the Hellriders.
forgotten-realms.rule.the-creed-resolute.blocked_reason: The passage describes a binding oath but gives no basic-grammar rule for enforcing or breaking it.

forgotten-realms.rule.mantol-derith-comm.name: Mantol-Derith commerce laws

effect.summary: The market chiefly forbids theft, magical influence over negotiations, and counterfeiting; violators are chained and thrown into the Darklake.

forgotten-realms.rule.mantol-derith-comm.go_wrong: Violators are sentenced on the spot.

forgotten-realms.rule.subrace-traits-in-.name: Subrace traits in the Realms

effect.summary: A subrace has its primary race’s traits plus its own; this book’s material takes precedence over the Player’s Handbook if they differ.

forgotten-realms.rule.subrace-traits-in-.cost_or_limit: Subrace-specific traits apply where they differ or replace primary-race traits.
forgotten-realms.rule.subrace-traits-in-.combines: Primary race traits and subrace traits

forgotten-realms.rule.duergar-magic.name: Duergar Magic

effect.summary: At level 3, cast enlarge/reduce on yourself using only enlarge; at level 5, cast invisibility on yourself once.

forgotten-realms.rule.duergar-magic.cost_or_limit: One use of each available spell, regained after a long rest; no material components; unavailable in direct sunlight.
forgotten-realms.rule.duergar-magic.who_may: Duergar meeting the stated level requirements

forgotten-realms.rule.sunlight-sensitivi.name: Sunlight Sensitivity

effect.summary: Direct sunlight hinders attacks and sight-dependent Wisdom checks involving the character or the target.

forgotten-realms.rule.sunlight-sensitivi.cost_or_limit: Disadvantage on affected attacks and checks in direct sunlight.

forgotten-realms.rule.option-human-langu.name: OPTION: HUMAN LANGUAGES

effect.summary: A human with an ethnicity-specific language may know it in addition to Common.

forgotten-realms.rule.option-human-langu.cost_or_limit: Applies if the DM permits the option and the ethnicity has its own language.
forgotten-realms.rule.option-human-langu.combines: Language choice is an additional free language.

forgotten-realms.rule.worship-that-is-de.name: worship that is deemed heretical or dangerous is outlawed

effect.summary: A ruling power may prohibit worship it considers dangerous.

forgotten-realms.rule.worship-that-is-de.cost_or_limit: Depends on local authority and doctrine.
forgotten-realms.rule.worship-that-is-de.combines: A region ruled by Shar's followers may outlaw Selûne worship.

forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-water-los.name: Moonwell water loses its properties outside the well

effect.summary: Water taken away from a moonwell or put in a container becomes ordinary water.

forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-water-los.cost_or_limit: Applies when containerized or carried more than 30 feet from the well.
forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-water-los.who_may: Applies to anyone carrying moonwell water.
forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-water-los.combines: Defines when the well’s healing or harmful properties cease.
forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-water-los.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward proximity and containment restriction.

forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-daily-eff.name: Moonwell daily effect limit

effect.summary: A drinker can receive a moonwell’s effect only once per day.

forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-daily-eff.cost_or_limit: Once per day for each drinker.
forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-daily-eff.combines: Limits either the healing or poison effect.
forgotten-realms.rule.moonwell-daily-eff.blocked_reason: This is a simple per-target usage limit.

forgotten-realms.rule.precepts-of-incand.name: Precepts of Incandescence

effect.summary: The order’s code urges bodily refinement, virtue, and bringing light into darkness.

forgotten-realms.rule.precepts-of-incand.cost_or_limit: Three principles: physical perfection, spiritual virtue, and shining light into darkness.
forgotten-realms.rule.precepts-of-incand.mind: Promotes virtue and recognition of goodness in others.
forgotten-realms.rule.precepts-of-incand.combines: Reflects ideas associated with Sune, Selûne, and Lathander.
forgotten-realms.rule.precepts-of-incand.blocked_reason: This is a roleplaying conduct rule, not a missing effect capability.

forgotten-realms.rule.warlocks-may-forge.name: Warlocks may forge multiple pacts but must favor one

effect.summary: A warlock can make several pacts but eventually must favor one because patrons are jealous.

forgotten-realms.rule.warlocks-may-forge.cost_or_limit: Must eventually choose a favored pact.
forgotten-realms.rule.warlocks-may-forge.go_wrong: Patrons may be possessive or jealous.

forgotten-realms.rule.wizardly-longevity.name: wizardly longevity

effect.summary: Great wizards can extend their lives far beyond the ordinary span of their race.

forgotten-realms.rule.wizardly-longevity.cost_or_limit: Lichdom is one route; no details stated
forgotten-realms.rule.wizardly-longevity.go_wrong: Lichdom involves withdrawal from the world in body and mind
forgotten-realms.rule.wizardly-longevity.mind: Lichdom is associated with mental withdrawal
forgotten-realms.rule.wizardly-longevity.blocked_reason: The passage describes extraordinary longevity and lichdom without specifying the character’s resulting soul or death state.

forgotten-realms.rule.inheritance-proper.name: Inheritance properties are determined by the story

effect.summary: An inheritance may be mundane, magical, gradually strengthen, or reveal its nature after conditions are met.

forgotten-realms.rule.inheritance-proper.cost_or_limit: The Dungeon Master determines its properties and history
forgotten-realms.rule.inheritance-proper.go_wrong: It may draw claimants or adversaries
forgotten-realms.rule.inheritance-proper.combines: May have a modest ability that increases over time or concealed properties
forgotten-realms.rule.inheritance-proper.blocked_reason: An inheritance can carry an ability whose details or growth are not defined by the basic effect grammar.
